errors.AUTH_FAILURE: Authentication failed. Check your username and password in sync settings.
errors.CREDENTIAL_INVALID: The sync server no longer accepts this device's sync access. Your changes are saved on this device. Ask whoever runs your sync server to restore access for this device.
errors.FORBIDDEN: Sync blocked (403). Your server may be blocking the request.
errors.LOCKED: Sync is locked by another device. Try again in a moment.
errors.NETWORK_ERROR: Network error. Check your connection and try again.
errors.PASSPHRASE_REQUIRED: Enter your sync passphrase to continue.
errors.QUOTA_EXCEEDED: The sync server has reached its limit for this account. Your changes are saved on this device and syncing will retry automatically. Ask whoever runs your sync server to raise the limit.
errors.KEY_MISMATCH: Wrong sync passphrase. It must exactly match the passphrase used on your other devices.
errors.VERIFIER_UNSUPPORTED: Your GLANCEvault server needs to be updated to support this app version (key verification).
errors.ACCOUNT_ID_REQUIRED: GLANCEvault is missing an account ID. Re-enter your GLANCEvault details (URL, device token, and account ID) in Cloud Sync settings.
errors.APP_ID_MISMATCH: This sync data belongs to a different app.
errors.SCHEMA_FORWARD_INCOMPATIBLE: This sync data is from a newer app version. Please update the app.
errors.passphraseNeeded: Enter your sync passphrase above to enable GLANCEvault.
errors.vaultUnreachable: Couldn't reach GLANCEvault. Check the vault URL and device token. ({{detail}})

vaultUrl.httpRejected: Insecure connection. Use https:// for a vault on the public internet. Plain http:// is only allowed on a trusted local network (localhost or a LAN address).
vaultUrl.insecureLanWarning: Unencrypted connection: only use on a trusted network.

form.webdavToggleHint: Sync to any WebDAV server (Nextcloud, ownCloud, etc.). Turn this off to keep your connection details but stop syncing on this device, for example when moving fully to GLANCEvault.
form.syncFolderHint: Path on your WebDAV server where sync files are stored.
form.migrationBody: Your sync file is at the old location. You can move it for cleaner organization, and sync will continue to work either way.
form.migrationInstruction: After moving the file, update your Sync folder setting above to
form.encryptionExplainer: Your data is encrypted on-device before upload. The server never sees your plaintext. Use a sync passphrase, not your WebDAV password.
form.encryptionAlreadyConfigured: Encryption is already configured. Leave the passphrase field blank to keep your existing key, or enter it again to re-authenticate on this device.
form.storePassphraseBody: This passphrase cannot be recovered. You will need it to set up sync on new devices. Store it in a password manager.
form.vaultExperimentalWarning: Experimental. Requires a self-hosted GLANCEvault server. Not recommended for most users.
form.vaultToggleHint: Row-grained database sync. Runs alongside your existing WebDAV sync. Your WebDAV data is never modified. Uses the same encryption passphrase as above.
form.vaultReloadHint: Saving a GLANCEvault change reloads the app so the sync engines reconstruct.
form.vaultNeedsEncryption: GLANCEvault is always end-to-end encrypted. Turn on "{{encryption}}" above and set your sync passphrase to enable it.
form.vaultNeedsPassphrase: Enter your sync passphrase in the encryption section above to enable GLANCEvault on this device.
form.vaultUnreachableSimple: Could not reach the vault at this URL.
form.vaultSkipped_one: {{count}} item couldn't be read (skipped). This usually means a different sync passphrase was used on another device.
form.vaultSkipped_other: {{count}} items couldn't be read (skipped). This usually means a different sync passphrase was used on another device.

sync.passphraseHint: This is the passphrase you set when you first enabled encryption. It is never stored — only you know it.
sync.passphrasePrompt: Cloud sync is encrypted. Enter your sync passphrase to continue.

settings.obsidianDailyNoteTemplateBridgeHint: Pre-filled when creating a new daily note. {{dateToken}} becomes the note's date. A template note configured in the Bridge plugin takes precedence when the plugin creates the note.
settings.glanceBackgroundPollHint: How often to check while the browser tab is hidden.
settings.glanceForegroundPollHint: How often to check for new events while the app is in the foreground.
settings.localIntegrationsDesc: Connections for other apps running on this computer. Both listen on 127.0.0.1 only and are never reachable from the network.
settings.localIntegrationsUnknownAction: The requested local-integration change is not supported ({{action}}).
settings.mcpAllowScheduleChangesDesc: Separate opt-in: connected apps may add, complete, move, and edit tasks.
settings.mcpConsentCalendarParagraph1: This adds events from your device’s calendar accounts (work, school, shared family calendars) to what connected apps can read, not just data you created in dayGLANCE.
settings.mcpConsentCalendarParagraph2: Calendar events often contain other people’s information: event titles, attendee names and emails, and details of meetings other people invited you to. You did not create that information, and those people have not agreed to share it with an AI assistant or any other app.
settings.mcpConsentCalendarParagraph3: Connected apps can read these events exactly like your dayGLANCE data, and typically send them to an AI provider over the internet.
settings.mcpConsentCalendarParagraph4: Leave this off to share only the data you created in dayGLANCE yourself.
settings.mcpConsentReadParagraph1: This lets other applications running on this computer, typically an AI assistant such as Claude Desktop, read your dayGLANCE data: your schedule, tasks, goals, and projects.
settings.mcpConsentReadParagraph2: AI assistants usually send what they read to their AI provider over the internet as part of your conversations. Once another app has read your data, dayGLANCE cannot see or control what it does with it.
settings.mcpConsentReadParagraph3: This is outside dayGLANCE’s encryption and no-server-access guarantees: dayGLANCE itself still never uploads your data anywhere, but an app you connect might.
settings.mcpConsentReadParagraph4: Only apps on this computer that present your access token (shown in settings after enabling) can connect.
settings.mcpConsentReadTitle: Allow other apps to read your dayGLANCE data?
settings.mcpConsentWritesParagraph1: Connected apps will be able to add, complete, move, and edit tasks (the same changes you can make yourself) without asking you before each one.
settings.mcpConsentWritesParagraph2: Changes are rate-limited and can never touch device calendar events, but a misbehaving app could still rearrange or complete tasks you did not intend. You can turn this off at any time.
settings.mcpConsentWritesTitle: Allow connected apps to change your schedule?
settings.mcpErrorCalendarConsentRequired: Accept the device-calendar notice before sharing calendar events.
settings.mcpErrorNoToken: Enable MCP before generating a new access token.
settings.mcpErrorPortEphemeral: Port 0 changes on every launch. Choose a fixed port from 1 to 65535.
settings.mcpErrorPortInvalid: The MCP port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535 (received {{value}}).
settings.mcpErrorPortRange: The MCP port must be between 1 and 65535 (received {{value}}).
settings.mcpErrorPortTypeInvalid: The MCP port has an invalid value type ({{type}}). Enter a whole number from 1 to 65535.
settings.mcpErrorReadConsentRequired: Accept the read-access notice before enabling MCP.
settings.mcpErrorReadTierRequired: Enable MCP read access before allowing schedule changes.
settings.mcpErrorUnknownReadTier: The requested MCP read level is not supported ({{tier}}).
settings.mcpErrorWritesConsentRequired: Accept the schedule-changes notice before allowing changes.
settings.mcpPortHint: Leave the port empty for the default. dayGLANCE never picks a different port by itself.
settings.mcpPortInUse: The MCP server could not start because port {{port}} is already in use. Choose a different fixed port in settings.
settings.mcpPortPermissionDenied: The MCP server was not allowed to use port {{port}} ({{error}}). Ports below 1024 may require elevated privileges; choose a higher port.
settings.mcpReadCalendarDesc: Everything above, plus events from your device calendar accounts (marked read-only).
settings.mcpReadDayglanceDesc: Schedule, tasks, goals, and projects you created in dayGLANCE. Device calendar events are excluded.
settings.mcpReadOffDesc: No MCP server runs and no port is opened.
settings.mcpRotateTokenTitle: Generate a new token. The old one stops working immediately.
settings.mcpServerBindFailed: The MCP server could not start on port {{port}}: {{error}}
settings.mcpServerDesc: Lets AI assistants on this computer read your schedule over the Model Context Protocol. What they can see is up to you:
settings.mcpServerStartFailed: The MCP server could not start. See the startup log for details.
settings.mcpStatusOffUndoAvailable: The server was turned off, but changes MCP clients made this session can still be undone.
settings.mcpStatusSessionNoChanges: No changes by MCP this session
settings.mcpStatusTurnOffFailed: Could not turn the server off.
settings.mcpStatusTurnOffTitle: Turn the MCP server off. No apps will be able to connect until you re-enable it in Settings.
settings.mcpStatusUndoAllTitle: Reverse every change MCP clients made since dayGLANCE started (or since the last undo). Undone new tasks go to the recycle bin.
settings.mcpStatusUndoTaskTitle: Reverse the changes MCP clients made to this task, restoring its state before MCP first touched it. An undone new task goes to the recycle bin.
settings.mcpStatusWritesAutoDisabled: Writes were auto-disabled after repeated rate-limit violations. Restart dayGLANCE to re-enable them.
settings.mcpSetupAdded: dayGLANCE entry added. Everything else in the file was preserved.
settings.mcpSetupBackup: A backup of the previous file was saved next to it.
settings.mcpSetupBridgeMissing: This build did not ship the bridge, so nothing was written. Install the bridge yourself with "npx -y @glance-apps/mcp-bridge", then follow the setup guide to point Claude Desktop at it. Please report this build as broken.
settings.mcpSetupClaudeTitle: Adds a dayGLANCE entry to Claude Desktop's configuration, pointing at the bridge bundled with this app. Everything else in the file is preserved, and a backup is made first.
settings.mcpSetupGuidePrefix: To connect Claude Desktop or other MCP apps, see the
settings.mcpSetupGuideSuffix: . You will paste the access token above into your MCP client.
settings.mcpSetupUnavailable: dayGLANCE could not run setup at all, so nothing was written. This is a fault in the app rather than in your configuration. Restart dayGLANCE, and if it persists, set the bridge up by hand with "npx -y @glance-apps/mcp-bridge" and please report the build.
settings.mcpSetupUnparseable: Your Claude Desktop configuration file could not be parsed, so dayGLANCE did not touch it. To finish setup by hand, fix or empty the file, or paste this entry into it:
settings.mcpSetupWriteFailed: The configuration could not be written automatically. To finish setup by hand, paste this entry into your Claude Desktop configuration file:
settings.mcpTokenHint: Paste this into your MCP client as the Bearer token. Rotating it cuts off every client using the old one.
settings.mcpTokenRotatedHint: New token generated. The old one no longer works, so update your MCP clients.
settings.streamDeckPortInUse: Port {{port}} is already in use. The Stream Deck plugin requires this port, so quit the conflicting process, then turn Stream Deck support off and on.
settings.streamDeckSupportDesc: Lets the dayGLANCE Stream Deck plugin show and control your day (port {{port}}).
settings.obsidianNoVaultConfigured: No vault configured. Open settings to select your Obsidian vault folder.
settings.obsidianTaskHeadingHint: Markdown heading under which new tasks are appended in daily notes.
settings.resetTestPurchaseWarning: This permanently revokes this account's lifetime purchase from Google Play. It is not a refresh and cannot be undone. It has no effect on subscriptions: cancel in Google Play and let the subscription expire instead. For internal testing only.

settings.syncCalendarCreds: Sync calendar credentials across my devices
settings.syncCalendarCredsNeedsEncryption: Takes effect once sync encryption is on. Until then, credentials stay on this device.
settings.importIcsDesc: Import events from an iCal (.ics) file
settings.multiUserModeHint: Tag chores with specific household members
settings.multiUserRequiresSync: Requires cloud sync. Set up GLANCEvault or WebDAV sync first.
settings.obsidianLaunchOnWriteHint: After dayGLANCE writes to your vault, launch Obsidian so Obsidian Sync can push the change to your other devices. On macOS this happens in the background.
settings.obsidianLaunchOnWriteHintAndroid: After dayGLANCE writes to your vault, leaving the app with Back opens Obsidian directly; leaving with Home or Recents shows a notification you can tap instead (Android doesn't let apps open over the Home screen). Either way, Obsidian Sync can then push the change to your other devices.
settings.obsidianCompletionDatesHint: When you complete a task, its completion date is added to the task line in your vault, as ✅ 2026-01-15 when the Tasks plugin is enabled, or as a [completed:: …] Dataview field otherwise. Turning this off stops new markers; existing lines are left untouched until they next change.
settings.obsidianCompletionLog: Log completions to your daily notes
settings.obsidianCompletionLogHint: Every task you complete is recorded as a permanent line in that day's daily note, with its completion time, project, and tags. Entries stay even if you uncomplete the task. The log uses its own line format so it never re-imports as a task.
settings.obsidianBridgeActiveMode: Bridge plugin active (paired {{days}} days ago). Direct vault access disabled.
settings.obsidianBridgeActiveModeToday: Bridge plugin active (paired today). Direct vault access disabled.
settings.obsidianBridgeActiveModeUnknown: Bridge plugin active. Direct vault access disabled.
settings.obsidianBridgeRunning: Plugin heartbeat detected: not paired yet.
settings.obsidianBridgeNotDetected: No plugin heartbeat: install the dayGLANCE Bridge plugin in this vault and open Obsidian.
settings.obsidianBridgeWaiting: Obsidian is not running on this device. Your tasks still sync between devices as usual. Edits that touch your notes are queued and written to the vault when Obsidian runs with the bridge plugin on any paired device.
settings.obsidianBridgeWaitingNeverSeen: Obsidian has not synced with the plugin on this device yet.
settings.obsidianBridgeStampingNoConfig: The plugin is waiting for its configuration from dayGLANCE. Task import from daily notes is paused until it arrives (usually under a minute).
settings.obsidianBridgeStampingArmed: Automatic block IDs: active. The plugin stamps new task lines before reporting them.
settings.obsidianBridgeStampingOff: Automatic block IDs: off. The plugin reports notes without stamping new task lines.
settings.obsidianBridgeHint: Pair the dayGLANCE Bridge plugin in this vault with your GLANCEvault server. The pairing offer travels only through your vault folder, sealed under a one-time code shown here. Pairing again mints a fresh code and rotates the bridge key. Use that to re-pair after revoking a token.
settings.obsidianBridgeTokenHint: Prefilled with this device's GLANCEvault token. On a shared-token server the bridge uses the same one. Replace it only if you run a separate credential for the bridge.
settings.obsidianBridgeCodeHint: In Obsidian, run the command “dayGLANCE Bridge: Enter pairing code” and type this code. The offer expires after 10 minutes.
settings.obsidianBridgePairedOnce: Pairing happens once, from a desktop with direct vault access, and covers every device that opens this vault, including this one.
settings.obsidianBridgeUnpairedHere: The bridge plugin is running here but is not paired on this device. Tasks on this device are using direct vault access.
settings.obsidianBridgeUnpairedVaultPaired: This vault is already paired, so the plugin on this device has lost its credentials.
settings.obsidianBridgeUnpairedRemediation: Known cause: Obsidian Sync stopped syncing community plugin settings. In Obsidian's Sync settings on this device, make sure plugin settings sync is turned on. The pairing travels in the plugin's settings file and cannot reach this device without it.
settings.obsidianBridgeUnpairedVaultUnpaired: This vault has not been paired yet. Pair it once from a desktop device.

settings.calendarUrlHelpPrompt: Where do I find these URLs?
settings.calendarUrlHelp: Paste any public ICS/iCal URL. Google Calendar: Settings → [your calendar] → “Secret address in iCal format”. Outlook: Settings → View all → Calendar → Shared calendars → Publish → ICS link. Nextcloud (public): Calendar → Settings → Copy the public link. Nextcloud (private): use the internal CalDAV URL with ?export appended (for example …/remote.php/dav/calendars/user/personal/?export) and enter credentials.
settings.aiOllamaConnectionError: Could not reach Ollama. Make sure it's running and CORS is enabled for this origin. See setup guide →
settings.aiOllamaCors: CORS must be enabled for this site's origin
settings.aiOllamaRunning: Ollama must be running on your computer
settings.calDAVSyncHint: For syncing completions back: the CalDAV collection URL (without ?export). In Nextcloud, the calendar ID in the URL may differ from the display name.
settings.deviceCalendarDescription: Calendar events are read from your device accounts. Use the Device Calendars section below to choose which calendars to show.
settings.deviceCalendarFilterHint: Uncheck to hide calendars. Leave all checked to show everything.
settings.glanceEncryptionEnabledHint: Uses your cloud sync passphrase. Set up once; remains active across sessions.

settings.glanceEventsPathHint: Path on the WebDAV server where event files are stored.

settings.glanceRetentionHint: Event files older than this are deleted automatically.

settings.glanceVaultIntentsHint: Independent of WebDAV intents and of GLANCEvault sync. Saving reloads the app so the poller restarts.
settings.glanceVaultPassphrasePrompt: GLANCEvault intents are always encrypted. Enter your sync passphrase to set up the encryption key.
settings.intentsPassphraseSetupHint: Required once to derive the intents encryption key. After this, no passphrase is needed across sessions.
settings.intentsPassphraseSetupTitle: Enter your sync passphrase to complete setup
settings.keepPastEventsHint: Older imported events are dropped to save storage. Future events are always kept.
settings.multiUserDescription: Share dayGLANCE with your household. Tasks can be assigned to specific people; unassigned tasks are visible to everyone.
settings.noDeviceCalendars: No calendars loaded — tap Refresh, or rebuild the app if this persists.
settings.obsidianBrowserRequirement: Obsidian integration requires a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, or Brave). Firefox and Safari do not support the File System Access API.
settings.obsidianBrowserUnsupported: Your browser does not support the File System Access API. Please use a Chromium-based browser (e.g., Chrome, Edge, Brave) to connect an Obsidian vault.
settings.obsidianDailyNoteTemplateHint: Pre-filled when creating a new daily note
settings.obsidianDailyNotesFolderHint: Leave empty for vault root. Common: "Daily Notes" or "journals"
settings.obsidianFilenamePatternHint: Date pattern for daily note filenames (without .md). e.g. "yyyy-MM-dd", "dd-MM-yyyy", "MMMM dd, yyyy"

backup.title: Backup & Restore
backup.description: Export your data to a file or restore from a previous backup.

backup.lastWriteFailed: The last backup write failed — check that the folder still exists and is writable.
backup.snapshotDescription: The live copy is updated within seconds of every change; snapshots are extra point-in-time files kept on this cadence.
backup.remoteDeviceHint: Only enable on one device. If you use multiple devices, use Cloud Sync to keep them in sync and set up remote backups on your primary device only.
